claim_verdicts.evidence: SemVer 2.0.0 summary: "Given a version number MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, increment the: 1. MAJOR version when you make incompatible API changes, 1. MINOR version when you add functionality in a backwards-compatible manner, and 1. PATCH version when you make backwards-compatible bug fixes." Rules 6-8 restate this as MUST for x > 0.
claim_verdicts.source: github.com/semver/semver semver.md @ tag v2.0.0 (gh api), Summary and rules 6-8

claim_verdicts.evidence: Rule 7: "Patch version MUST be reset to 0 when minor version is incremented." Rule 8: "Patch and minor version MUST be reset to 0 when major version is incremented."

Rule 2: "X, Y, and Z are non-negative integers, and MUST NOT contain leading zeroes... Each element MUST increase numerically. For instance: 1.9.0 -> 1.10.0 -> 1.11.0." Rule 11: "Major, minor, and patch versions are always compared numerically. Example: 1.0.0 < 2.0.0 < 2.1.0 < 2.1.1."
Rule 1: "Software using Semantic Versioning MUST declare a public API. This API could be declared in the code itself or exist strictly in documentation."
Rule 4: "Major version zero (0.y.z) is for initial development. Anything may change at any time. The public API should not be considered stable." Rule 5: "Version 1.0.0 defines the public API."

Rule 6: "Patch version Z (x.y.Z | x > 0) MUST be incremented if only backwards compatible bug fixes are introduced. A bug fix is defined as an internal change that fixes incorrect behavior." Lesson applies it only past 1.0.0 (API at 1.4.2), so the x > 0 condition holds.

Rule 7: MINOR "MUST be incremented if new, backwards compatible functionality is introduced to the public API." Rule 8: MAJOR "MUST be incremented if any backwards incompatible changes are introduced to the public API." Adding /api/v2 while /api/v1 is unchanged is new compatible functionality; removing /api/v1 is incompatible.

Lesson now keeps the condition: "not checked by any tool unless the team adds one. Whoever makes a release decides which part goes up". The spec defines rules only and puts correction on the releaser: FAQ "As soon as you realize that you've broken the Semantic Versioning spec, fix the problem and release a new minor version".
claim_verdicts.source: semver.md @ v2.0.0 (gh api repos/semver/semver), FAQ 'accidentally release a backwards incompatible change as a minor version'

claim_verdicts.evidence: Rule 3: "Once a versioned package has been released, the contents of that version MUST NOT be modified. Any modifications MUST be released as a new version." Rule 7: MINOR "MAY be incremented if substantial new functionality or improvements are introduced within the private code"; rule 8 MAJOR only for incompatible public API changes. So an invisible change needs a new number, MINOR only optionally: "normally a PATCH" is consistent.

Rule 8: MAJOR "MUST be incremented if any backwards incompatible changes are introduced to the public API. It MAY include minor and patch level changes." Rule 7: MINOR "MAY include patch level changes." Rule 9 defines pre-release ("MAY be denoted by appending a hyphen"); lesson only says it skips them, per depth_notes.

issues.text: Rule 1 requires software using SemVer to declare a public API at every version, 0.y.z included; rule 5 says 1.0.0 "defines the public API" and FAQ ties 1.0.0 to "a stable API on which users have come to depend". 'First release that declares' implies 0.y.z has no declared API, contradicting rule 1 and the lesson's own 'numbers only mean something against a declared public API'.
issues.fix: Write: "Version 1.0.0 is the release whose public API the team promises to keep; from then on every breaking change costs a MAJOR." No ledger change needed (claim 5 already cites rule 5).
issues.quote: Version 1.0.0 is the first release that declares the public API and promises to keep it
